title: Enterprise onboarding: integration, escalation, health checks & QBR playbook
author: Leah Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates our standard approach for enterprise onboarding covering integration checklists, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and the cadence and template for health checks and QBRs. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Product Engineering stakeholders who run or support customer migrations to Redwood Inference.

Purpose

- Provide a repeatable, low-risk path from legal/contract signature to sustained production usage.
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference and mean-time-to-resolution (MTTR) for customer-facing issues.
- Establish a shared set of expectations for SLAs, operational handoffs, and QBR content.

Scope

Applies to: Hosted/Redwood Dedicated/Private deployment onboarding for enterprise customers. Excludes internal proof-of-concept (POC) sandbox accounts unless explicitly adopted by CS.

Owners and Contacts

- Playbook owner: Customer Success (CS) Ops
- Primary CS contact: Leah Chen (author) — leah.chen@redwood.example.com
- Solutions Engineering: SE engagement lead (assigned per account)
- Escalation engineering on-call: eng-platform/escalations (see /eng-platform/runbooks)
- Support: Tier 1 and Tier 2 contacts listed in support roster (monthly sync)

Onboarding phases (high level)

1) Pre-boarding (contract -> kickoff)
   - Contract signed and account/provisioning details collected via onboarding intake form.
   - Create Jira onboarding epic with milestones: network setup, API keys, integration, validation, go-live, QBR schedule.
   - Assign stakeholders: CS, SE, Support, Customer IT, Security.

2) Integration & Validation (SE-led)
   - Integration checklist (minimum):
     - Confirm network connectivity (VPC peering or allowed IPs) and firewall rules.
     - API key creation and role-based access controls (RBAC) configured.
     - Model selection and traffic profiles documented (expected qps, token lengths).
     - Test prompts and evaluation set uploaded for quality verification.
     - Observability hooks enabled (tracing, logs, cost tags).
   - Validation tests (pass/fail):
     - Authentication and basic API call: curl GET /v1/health -> 200 OK.
     - Latency smoke test: 95th percentile latency for small prompts < 300ms (hosted) or target agreed SLA.
     - Token accounting: embeddings and generation usage recorded and visible in console.

Integration checklist (detailed)

- Networking
  - Confirm: customer CIDR list and egress rules.
  - Commands: customer-run traceroute to api.redwood.example.com; sample firewall allow rule:
    - iptables example (customer on-prem):
      sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d api.redwood.example.com --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

- Authentication & Secrets
  - Create API key in Console -> Access -> API keys.
  - Verify key works:
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/engines | jq .

- Observability
  - Ensure request_id and trace_id propagated.
  - Provide customer instructions for sending traces to our tracing intake if requested (link to /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts).

- Model & Performance
  - Confirm model variant, quantization profile, and target sequence length.
  - Run benchmark harness (SE-run): /scripts/benchmark_inference.sh --model <model> --qps 10 --duration 2m

- Security & Compliance
  - Validate data residency settings and KMS integration for Private deployments.
  - Collect customer's compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO) and map to our evidence artifacts.

Go-live steps

1. Final smoke test with customer traffic pattern (run 1 hour ramp).
2. Observe SLOs: error rate < 0.5%, 95p latency below agreed SLA, cost per 1k tokens within forecast +/- 20%.
3. CS announces go-live in the onboarding Jira epic and schedules 1-week hypercare.
4. SE hands off to Support/CS with runbook and escalation contacts.

Escalation playbook (incident routing & steps)

Severity definitions (use these for routing and SLA measurements):

| Severity | Definition | Business Impact | Initial Response SLA | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| P1 / Sev0 | Production outage: system unavailable for >= minimal functionality (customers cannot make inference calls) | Critical revenue / compliance impact | 1 hour | On-call Engineering + CS lead |
| P2 / Sev1 | Degraded: high error rates or severe performance regression impacting multiple customers | Major impact, partial mitigation | 4 hours | Escalation Eng + SE |
| P3 / Sev2 | Single-customer issue, non-blocking, or intermittent errors | Limited impact | 1 business day | Support Tier 2 |
| P4 / Sev3 | Low-impact, feature request, or documentation gaps | No immediate business impact | 3 business days | Support Tier 1 |

Immediate steps when a customer raises an issue:

1) Triage (Support Tier 1)
   - Acknowledge within SLA. Collect: customer environment, API key, request_id(s), timestamps, example payloads, and any recent config changes.
   - Run pre-flight checks: stack status page, host health, recent deploys, capacity alerts.

2) Reproduce and isolate (Support Tier 2 / SE)
   - Attempt to reproduce using customer's inputs. If reproducible, capture trace_id, logs, and kernel schedule.
   - If causes indicate infra/capacity, escalate to Eng-SRE immediately.

3) Escalate to Eng (if P1/P2)
   - Open an internal incident channel (Slack #incidents/<customer>-<YYYYMMDD>). Post summary, severity, impact, and requested owner.
   - Eng on-call takes ownership of mitigation. If deployment rollback required, follow /eng-serving-runtime/release-notes rollback steps.

4) Communication
   - CS provides customer-facing updates every 1 hour for P1, every 4 hours for P2, and daily for P3 until resolved. Use standard update template (see below).

Incident update template (customer-facing)

- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Summary: Short summary of impact
- Scope: Affected endpoints/customers
- What we know: Observed symptoms and preliminary root cause if known
- Actions taken: Steps the team is performing now
- ETA / next update: next scheduled update time
- Contact: CS lead name and escalation channel

Known issues and workarounds (current list)

1) Tokenization drift with older tokenizer versions
   - Symptom: Off-by-one token counts when customers convert tokens on their side, causing occasional truncation of output.
   - Workaround: Ensure tokenizer library >= 0.9.2. SE-run script: pip install --upgrade redwood-tokenizer>=0.9.2

2) Intermittent 502s during large-model rolling upgrades (observed 2026-03)
   - Symptom: Short spikes of 502s for a small subset of requests during rolling kernel updates.
   - Mitigation: Enable automatic retry (idempotent requests) at client SDK: retry=3, backoff=exponential(200ms). For non-idempotent flows, route to compatible lower-latency model variant until upgrade completes.

3) Misattributed cost in Console for multi-tenant Dedicated deployments
   - Symptom: Token costs attributed to default project when customer uses legacy API key mapping.
   - Workaround: Re-map API keys to explicit project IDs using Console -> Billing -> API key mapping. Contact billing@redwood.example.com if mapping API is required.

Support process and SLAs

- Channels
  - Primary: Support portal (support.redwood.example.com) — creates ticket in Zendesk/Jira.
  - Secondary: Email to enterprise-support@redwood.example.com (only for customers with email-based escalation enabled).
  - Urgent: Dedicated Slack channel or phone bridge (provided in enterprise contract).

- SLAs (enterprise entitlements)
  - Response SLAs by severity (see severity table above).
  - Escalation SLA: For any P1 not acknowledged in 30 minutes, CS sends notification to Eng leadership and Customer Success director.

- Support handoffs
  - SE -> Support: Handoff doc includes integration checklist, validation logs, custom prompts, model config, and runbook for common issues.
  - Support -> CS: For any account trending toward contract expansion or churn risk, open an account health ticket.

Health checks and QBRs

- Health check cadence
  - Weekly (first 30 days post go-live): CS/SE sync with customer for usage, errors, and performance.
  - Monthly (30+ days): Health summary report and open action items.
  - Quarterly: Formal QBR covering product, ops, and roadmap alignment.

- Health check metrics (minimum set)
  - Usage: avg daily requests, peak qps, tokens/day, cost per 1k tokens.
  - Reliability: error rate (1h, 24h), MTTR for P1/P2 incidents, uptime (30d).
  - Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route.
  - Quality: regressions measured on customer evaluation set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity or pass/fail for structured outputs).
  - Security & compliance: audit log completeness, key rotation status, KMS access logs.

- QBR template (high level)
  1. Executive summary (top-line health and asks)
  2. Adoption & usage trends (growth and forecast)
  3. Reliability & performance (incidents, SLOs, improvements)
  4. Cost & optimization opportunities (batching, quantization recommendations)
  5. Roadmap & product asks (feature requests and prioritization)
  6. Action items and owners (with deadlines)

Deliverables and artifacts

- Onboarding epic (Jira): milestone checklist and acceptance criteria.
- SE validation folder: benchmark results, smoke test logs, and prompt evaluation set.
- Customer runbook: exported PDF included in handoff to Support.
- QBR slides: standard template (share via Google Slides link in related_pages).

Appendices

A: Troubleshooting -- quick commands
- Check service health: curl -s https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health | jq .status
- Pull trace by request: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/traces/<trace_id>
- Collect logs for timeframe (example):
  - journalctl -u redwood-inference -S "2026-05-01 00:00:00" -U "2026-05-01 01:00:00" > /tmp/redwood-logs.txt

B: Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who approves model changes in production?
  - A: Model change requests from customers require SE sign-off and CS confirmation; production rollouts follow eng-serving-runtime ADR 2025-11 (see related pages).

C: Escalation contacts (short list)
- CS Director: Maya Thompson (maya.thompson@redwood.example.com)
- Eng SRE Lead: Omar Singh (omar.singh@redwood.example.com)
- On-call escalation channel: #incidents (Slack)
